Generate a professional environment visual reference sheet, not a single empty shot or a basic three-view layout. The sheet is a layout for spatial evidence, not an instruction to default to concept art, illustration, or any other medium.

[APPROVED SCENE DESCRIPTION]
{scene_description}

[FIXED CHARACTER SLOTS]
{available_slots}

[BACKGROUND CROWD POLICY]
{crowd_policy}

[PROJECT ART STYLE]
{art_style}

First read the selected style's medium/rendering method, material language, color, lighting, and negative constraints, then use that same medium for every view. Never default to environment concept art, a 3D game scene, or live-action photography: live-action/photographic, 2D animation/comic, 3D animation, and other styles each retain their own image-making logic. The grid, floor plan, and axonometric view organize information only and must not alter the project style of the principal views. When an example conflicts with the project style, the project style wins.

Use one 16:9 landscape multi-view grid. Every panel shows the same scene, time, and design. Include: 01 master wide, 02 left view, 03 right view, 04 reverse view, 05 bird's-eye view, 06 key spatial anchor close-up, 07 exterior or establishing view, 08 main entrance view, and 09 circulation/depth perspective. If no independent exterior exists, use an interior/exterior entrance connection for 07 instead of inventing a facade. Also include a concise floor plan, axonometric view, palette swatches, and 3–5 key material or fixed-object studies.

Keep floor plan, architecture, doors, windows, circulation, object count and scale, materials, palette, light direction, and period identical across views. Every available-slot anchor must be visible with usable open space. Follow crowd_policy for an empty set or anonymous background crowd only. Exclude named characters, plot action, speech bubbles, poster composition, random furniture changes, and contradictory layouts. Never replace the selected project style with a more common but mismatched concept-art, photographic, painted-2D, or 3D-rendered treatment.
